contract: Both arms receive the same bounded candidate programs and learn/validate instrument calibration from two purchased reset trajectories before planning. The true response gain and instrument law stay in the apparatus. Window candidates include gains1/2 plus zero; event candidates also include instantaneous alternatives. On the fourth task, the physical instrument changes after initial calibration; both arms observe the resulting calibration failure, acquire and validate a replacement mapping, then replan. The real planner, acquisition, full hypothesis assessment, method observation and complete KnowledgeLibrary JSON restore execute between tasks. Source synthesis, replay, all observations, failed forecasts and recalibration costs are counted. Independent random plus activation/exit terminal trajectories run only after all learning. This is a controlled component sequence with supplied candidate families, not full Unified family invention. Development retains the original five stages. Before dispatch, formal sequences add a sixth visit to the previously repaired instrument, with its changed negative gain and delay active from the first purchased calibration trajectory. The first five stages and all budgets stay unchanged. A locally revised preparation is counted as supported only after real observation creates its parent-linked method; subsequent use and return-source use are counted from actual method feedback, never inferred from successful proposals.
baseline_development_note: Reuse the completed five-stage 0.76 development algorithm snapshot. Final 0.76 differs only in metadata and the compound current/history identity branch; this simple-window/event protocol does not exercise that branch. No old development or old formal tasks are rerun.
